paper_title: New Limits on Exotic Spin-Dependent Interactions at Astronomical Distances
notes: This paper constrains exotic spin-dependent interactions (scalar-pseudoscalar, vector-axial-vector, and axial-axial-vector) at astronomical ranges using comagnetometer data. The constraints are on PRODUCTS of vertex couplings (e.g., g_N^S × g_n^P, g_N^V × g_n^A, g_N^A × g_n^A) where N and n denote nucleon and neutron respectively. These product couplings do not correspond to the canonical AxionLimitBench coupling types, which are single couplings (g_aγγ, g_ae, g_an, g_ap, etc.). The bounds are derived from reinterpreting existing Lorentz and CPT violation constraints rather than from dedicated axion/ALP searches. Main results: For λ > 10^12 m: |g_N^S g_n^P| < 1.6×10^-35, |g_N^V g_n^A| < 7.1×10^-59, |g_N^A g_n^A| < 8.1×10^-31 (95% C.L.). The interaction ranges of 10^6 to 10^14 m correspond to mediator masses of ~10^-20 to 10^-12 eV.
